stimuli.description: An office common area with plants, bamboo floor, and external views of green space and a river (biophilic environment), and a classroom without windows or indoor plants (non-biophilic environment).
Immersive 360-degree field-of-view videos of the same biophilic and non-biophilic environments.

limitations: Participants were young healthy adults, potentially leading to selection bias and limited generalizability.
Study included only two environmental conditions (low BIDI=3, moderate BIDI=27), potentially underestimating impacts compared to environments with more biophilic components.

Study conducted in a building with good air quality and thermal comfort, preventing parsing of effects to single natural elements or interactions with other indoor environmental quality factors (e.g., noise, odors, lighting).

Observed differences in baseline physiological measures between visits, despite randomization and control for between-visit variables, potentially affecting physiological and cognitive changes during the experiment.
Participants were not blinded to the test environments, potentially leading to biased estimates of effects on performance.
